churn_resistance.rationale: A framework upgrade would touch only server.js, document.ts, vite.config.ts and the defineRoute call sites — data, logic and types are fully decoupled. Deductions: the build-step guard encodes undocumented Gracile build behavior and is copy-pasted into five route files, and the sprite URL pattern is a second place the app assumes API internals.

findings.issue: The POKEDEX_BUILD_STEP flag encodes an undocumented Gracile behavior (handlers are invoked once during `vite build` to render document shells), and the guard is repeated in five route files ((home).ts:14, pokemon/[name].ts:92, abilities/[name].ts:13, moves/[name].ts:14, types/[name].ts:13).
findings.suggestion: Keep the flag but centralize it: a single `routeHandler(loader)` helper (or default-empty props inside lib/data.ts) instead of per-route if-blocks, and note the assumption in a comment so a future Gracile release providing an official build-time signal can replace it in one place.

findings.issue: Switching games fetches a full HTML page and DOMParser-extracts the `[data-move-tables]` fragment, coupling the client script to server markup and re-downloading a large document per selection.
findings.suggestion: Serve move tables (or game moves as JSON) from a route endpoint like the existing api/species-index.ts, so the client depends on data, not on HTML structure.

findings.issue: Stale-response guards are ticket counters (`latest`, `ticket`); superseded fetches are never cancelled (same in app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:37-45 and app/src/lib/api.ts:49-53, which has no timeout either).
findings.suggestion: Use AbortController per interaction (abort on new input) and an AbortSignal.timeout() on the server-side fetch.

findings.issue: Sprite URLs are constructed from the documented `/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` pattern instead of the API's own sprite fields, so a change in the API's media layout would silently break every card image.
findings.suggestion: Where a Pokémon record is already fetched (e.g. the Pokémon page), prefer the API-provided URL and fall back to the pattern; keep the pattern only where it is the pragmatic win (the 1025-card index).

findings.issue: @types/express is a devDependency but server.js is plain JavaScript and app/tsconfig.json:3 only includes `src` and vite.config.ts, so the types are never consumed.
findings.suggestion: Drop @types/express, or type-check server.js by adding it to the tsconfig include.

summary: This is a forward-thinking app I'd hold up as an example for this stack: every Gracile, Lit, Vite and TypeScript API matches the current stable docs (verified 2026-10-30), dependency hygiene is near-perfect, and progressive enhancement over native forms keeps the JS surface tiny. Data access, types and templates are factored so a framework upgrade touches only a handful of files. The one real aging risk is the POKEDEX_BUILD_STEP guard, which encodes undocumented build behavior and is repeated across five routes.
